data.narrative: Completed Module 2 Prompt Decomposition - chose top-down decomposition approach to catch cross-cutting concerns before execution, then refine progressively. Created task tree with 8 medium-grained tasks for Team Collaboration feature. Wrote first 3 prompts in full text with specific field definitions. Verified Task 1 prompt against acceptance criteria - output matched, no red flags, reproducible. Identified conflicting assumption in BREAK: Task 1 lacked owner_id but Task 2 assumed role-based ownership. Fixed by adding interface contracts to task tree and updating Task 1 prompt to include owner_id. Learned atomic task principle, 60/40 decomposition rule, interface contracts prevent conflicts.

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote specific, constrained prompts with exact field definitions, conventions, and constraints. Task 1 prompt specified exact Team model fields (id, name, description, owner_id, created_at, updated_at) with types and constraints. Prompt included which files to reference, conventions to follow, and what not to do (no new fields, no new packages). Two different agents would produce substantially similar output.
dimension_scores.evidence: prompts-1-3.md: 'The Team model should have these exact fields: id: UUID, primary key, default=uuid4(), name: String, required, maximum 100 characters, description: String, optional, maximum 500 characters, nullable, owner_id: UUID, foreign key to users.id, required'

dimension_scores.observation: Simulated Task 1 output and verified against all acceptance criteria. Checked for unspecified decisions agent made (migration file naming, as_uuid=True parameter) - both acceptable and follow patterns. Red flags check passed: no 'use best practices' in prompt, output is testable. Identified conflicting assumption between Task 1 and Task 2 (missing owner_id) that would cause architectural inconsistency.
dimension_scores.evidence: task-1-verification.md: 'Acceptance Criteria Verification: Run migration succeeds, Query database returns empty table with correct schema, Import model succeeds. Red Flags Check: No use best practices in prompt, error handling not required for this task, output is testable'

dimension_scores.observation: Caught decomposition bug in BREAK step after one verification cycle. Identified root cause as missing ownership concept in Task 1. Fixed by adding interface contracts to task tree and updating Task 1 prompt to include owner_id. This is 'fixable with better context' - the fix was in decomposition and prompt specification, not requiring multiple AI re-generations. Interface contracts prevent similar conflicts in future.
dimension_scores.evidence: task-2-break-analysis.md: 'Root cause: Decomposition missed ownership concept entirely. Task 1 should have included owner_id to establish team creator/owner. Without this, role-based access lacks foundation.'

dimension_scores.observation: Chose top-down decomposition over progressive for first pass to catch cross-cutting concerns (authentication, permissions, audit logging) before execution. Reasoning: progressive decomposition might discover in Task 6 that permissions should have existed since Task 1, requiring expensive retrofit. Chose medium-grained task granularity (8 tasks, 50-150 lines each) as sweet spot for review thoroughness and prompt efficiency. Recognized that decomposition quality directly predicts output quality.
dimension_scores.evidence: Decision: 'Decomposition approach: Top-Down for first pass to catch cross-cutting concerns. Team collaboration feature has cross-cutting concerns (authentication, permissions, audit logging) that touch every part of system. If I plan room by room progressively, I might discover in Task 6 that permissions should have existed since Task 1.'

dimension_scores.observation: Produced complete task tree with 8 tasks, each with task name, input context, expected output, acceptance criteria, and dependencies. Added interface contracts between dependent tasks defining what upstream produces and downstream expects. Written first 3 prompts in full text with specific constraints. Task 1 prompt verified to produce reproducible output matching acceptance criteria. Conflicting assumption fixed through interface contracts.
dimension_scores.evidence: task-tree.md: 'Interface Contract (produced for Task 2): Table: teams with columns id (UUID), name (string), owner_id (FK to users.id), description (string), created_at (timestamp), updated_at (timestamp). Every team has exactly one owner identified by owner_id.'

public_evidence.ability: Prompt decomposition - breaking feature specifications into atomic tasks with clear interfaces
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates critical AI engineering skill - decomposing vague feature specs into atomic, testable tasks with specific acceptance criteria and interface contracts. This prevents AI from making wrong assumptions and ensures generated code fits together. The 60/40 decomposition rule and interface contracts are essential for production-quality AI-augmented development.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Reflection: 'Task is atomic when acceptance criteria are obvious from outside. POST /teams returns 201 with team object is atomic. Implement team management is not. If you can't describe expected output in two sentences, task is too big.'

Reflection: 'Best AI engineers spend 60% on decomposition, 40% on everything else. Well-decomposed tasks produce usable output on first try. Vague tasks produce plausible garbage requiring five iterations.'

Reflection: 'Decomposition is not just splitting work - it's defining interfaces between pieces. Write down what each task produces and what dependent tasks expect. Interface contracts make conflicts visible before prompts run.'

learning_style_signals: values specificity in prompts over brevity
